title: Tomate Sauce
description: One of the five classic French mother sauces, prepared with tomatoes, mirepoix, herbs, and stock, creating a rich and versatile base for pasta, meat, poultry, seafood, and vegetable dishes.

ingredients.title: For the Tomate Sauce
items: Olive oil or pork fat – 2 tbsp
Freshly ground black pepper – to taste

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Mirepoix
steps: Heat the olive oil or pork fat in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery, then sauté until softened and aromatic.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook for about 1 minute.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Building the Sauce
steps: Add the peeled tomatoes and tomato paste (if using), then cook for several minutes until slightly thickened.
Pour in the stock or water and stir well to combine.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Slow Simmering
steps: Add the bay leaf, thyme, and pork rind if using.
Bring the sauce to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 45–60 minutes, stirring occasionally until rich and flavorful.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Finishing
steps: Remove the bay leaf, thyme, and pork rind.
Blend the sauce or pass it through a fine sieve for a smooth consistency, if desired.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper before serving.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Toss with pasta for a classic tomato-based dish.
Use as the base for Marinara, Spanish Sauce, or Bolognese.
Serve with grilled poultry, seafood, or roasted meats.
Pair with vegetables, eggs, or baked dishes such as lasagna and casseroles.

chefTips: Slow simmering develops a richer, sweeter tomato flavor.
Use ripe fresh tomatoes or premium canned tomatoes for the best results.
Blend and strain the sauce for a smooth, classic French finish.
Adjust the thickness by simmering longer or adding a little extra stock if needed.
Tomate Sauce is one of the five classic French mother sauces and serves as the foundation for many traditional tomato-based sauces.
